audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows were inverted relative to the packet and the mirror, while the whys[] on the same page already told the packet's story.
audit.why: Packet chart is Warwick, Graves, Skill, Skill, Warwick, Graves, Warwick at 53.25% over 1538 games, and the mirror audit (graves__warwick) set all seven of its rows to that same chart. whys[0..6] here already read Warwick / Graves / even / skill / Warwick / Graves / Warwick — only the side tokens disagreed.
audit.corrected: All six rows flipped on both layers as one atomic group with ratings rescaled to 7/3/5/5/7/3/7. diff moved from TRICKY to EVEN and diffRating from 7.5/10 to 5.5/10 to match a 53.25% win rate and a chart Warwick leads.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item stage was explained as 'his shotgun hits like a truck' with no mechanism, and Level 6 as generic 'point-and-click fight starter' boilerplate.
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16/15/14/13/12s but hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers its cooldown and refreshes the resistance boost — so on his item spike it is rarely down when you want it. End of the Line is 13s at rank 1 and detonates on terrain. Infinite Duress's 1.5s suppression is the only thing in Warwick's kit that stops the kite.
audit.corrected: Written into spikes[2], breakdown.cooldowns, phases[4].why, whys[5] and early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four places call Smoke Screen a blind (spikes[1], spikes[2], whys[4], whys[5], wants.foe[1]), and spikes[3] calls Blood Hunt a reveal.
audit.why: Riot's text for Smoke Screen: a cloud that reduces sight range, with magic damage and a brief Move Speed reduction on impact — no blind, no miss chance. Blood Hunt senses enemies below 50% health and grants Move Speed toward and attack speed against them, tripling below 25%; 'reveal' is not in the text. The mirror agent flagged the Smoke-Screen-blinds error as template-level, recurring on every Graves matchup.
audit.corrected: Blind removed everywhere it appeared; Blood Hunt described by its real 50%/25% thresholds and its actual Move Speed / attack speed effect.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0].why described the level-1 sustain generically.
audit.why: The mirror found the reverse error on Graves's page — it told the reader to burst Warwick low, which is exactly where Eternal Hunger triples. Stating the 50%/25% thresholds on this side keeps the two pages consistent.

edits.after: This is Graves's window; his first item hits hard and every basic attack he lands lowers Quickdraw's cooldown, so it is rarely down when you want it. Play for jungle collapses instead of dueling him.

edits.before: You reclaim the edge late: Blood Hunt reveal and speed let you run any low Graves down and Infinite Duress locks his slippery kit, and a fed Warwick with lifesteal out-sustains his burst in extended fights.
edits.after: You reclaim the edge late: Blood Hunt gives Move Speed toward anyone under 50% health and attack speed against them, tripling under 25%, so the longer a fight runs the worse his burst looks against your healing.

edits.after: Level 1 is yours on raw sustain, but by 2 Graves spikes: End of the Line detonates after 1 second or on contact with terrain, so never fight him with a wall at your back. Hold back and farm until Jaws of the Beast is up.
